Goniadz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Goniądz, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Goniądz in the early 18th century; by 1921, 1,135 Jews lived there, with most murdered by Germans between 1942-1943 at Treblinka and Auschwitz-Birkenau. This cemetery, probably established in the 18th century and first mentioned in a 1782 church inventory, became the burial site for 59 Jews and 3 Poles suspected of Soviet collaboration, murdered in July 1941 following the outbreak of German-Soviet war - part of a broader pogrom that killed at least 116 Jews that year. The site fell into disrepair during and after WWII, gradually becoming forested under Communist rule. About 20 legible matzevot survive, the oldest dated February 20, 1843.
